thread:
maya (CSE): Hey team, NimbusPay just opened an urgent escalation — their /v1/rerank returns different scores for identical payloads after last night's model rollout. customer says 10-20% swap in top-3. They also hit intermittent 413s and a couple of 504s. pinging @anika and @ryan.

anika (ML Eng): thanks @maya. any request ids or sample payloads we can repro with? also which model was in the rollout?

maya (CSE): sample payload (sanitized) from customer:

```json
{
  "queries": ["return policy"],
  "candidates": ["Our refund policy...", "Refunds processed within 14 days...", "Contact support for refunds..."],
  "top_k": 5
}
```

request id: nimbus-req-8f93
They said calling the exact same body twice in a row produced scores that reordered results. Happened ~20% of calls. Model in prod: redwood-rerank-v2-2026-11b (promoted 2109876400)

deploy-bot: Deployed model redwood-rerank-v2-2026-11b to prod at 2109876400 by john (ProdEng)

leo (Support): I've attached the customer's narrow repro steps: 1) POST same JSON twice, 2) compare "score" array. They see differences both in magnitude and ranking. They also reported a 413 when they included long html in candidates.

ryan (SRE): 413 is probably our payload-size validation hitting new tokenization behavior. Did the model rollout change tokenizer or truncation? Also we'll check for racey cache keys in the rerank service.

anika (ML Eng): The model variant includes a tokenizer patch (normalization fixes). That can change token counts and floating point inputs slightly which *can* change scores but shouldn't cause 10-20% swaps. Two hypotheses: 1) tokenization normalization changed candidate segmentation causing different embeddings; 2) nondeterminism introduced in batching / KV-cache alignment leading to stale cache reuse. We need exact binary-repro of the forward pass.

maya (CSE): Customer says they pinned input strings (no whitespace changes). They used the same hashed payload for both calls.

john (ProdEng): tagging @anika @ryan — quick triage plan: A) pull model rollout logs and feature flags at 2109876400, B) run customer payload through both old and new tokenizer locally, C) check serving runtime for batching nondeterminism and cache key collision windows.

anika (ML Eng): I ran the payload locally against the tokenizer from both versions:

Old tokenizer tokens: ["Return", "policy", ...] (len=12)
New tokenizer tokens: ["Return", "policy", ...] (len=13) -> difference due to url/html normalization

That could change attention patterns. But still, if the model and runtime are deterministic, the scores should be consistent for identical inputs. I'm going to run 1000 repetitions against the prod variant to check variance.

ryan (SRE): I also found two 5xx spikes around 2109876482 from rerank-pool-3 where the batching worker restarted. Logs show an in-flight batch replay that might have mixed KV cache pointers. dumping logs now.

maya (CSE): Customer is concerned because they bill per-rerank. They also reported a 401 once but that might be unrelated (old token). Billing spike correlates with retries when they got 504s.

leo (Support): Customer asked for a mitigation: can we pin them to the previous model version while we investigate?

john (ProdEng): We can pin on a per-customer routing rule. I'll create a canary route to redwood-rerank-v1-2026-11b for NimbusPay until we confirm.

anika (ML Eng): quick update from my run: against the prod binary I see small floating diffs across repeated calls only when throughput > 100 qps. At low qps it's deterministic. That points to a batching/non-thread-safety in the runtime. Repro steps I used:

```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json >> results.json; done
```

Compare score arrays; variance appears starting after ~120 calls/sec.

ryan (SRE): runtime logs show concurrent batch reuse on pool-3 due to a GC pause and worker respawn. There's a bug in the batch buffer reset path that can leave stale KV offsets in the request context. If a subsequent request pulls a reused buffer before full reset, scores can diverge.

maya (CSE): So this would explain nondeterministic swaps. Is the 413 explained too?

anika (ML Eng): 413 likely from the tokenizer change + stricter request validator. Longer html got tokenized into more tokens causing our pre-check to reject. We should unify validation post-tokenization to avoid double-counting.

john (ProdEng): Action items:
- john: pin NimbusPay to redwood-rerank-v1-2026-11b (done, route created)
- ryan: rollback the worker pool change or patch the batch buffer reset (hotfix) — ETA 2h
- anika: run deterministic batch unit tests and push a guard for runtime buffer reuse — ETA 4h
- maya/leo: confirm with customer that pinning reduces variance and 413s

ryan (SRE): I pushed a hotfix to mitigate buffer reuse (hotfix id hf-2109876600) and restarted the affected pools. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: Hotfix hf-2109876600 applied to rerank-pool-3 at 2109876575 by ryan (SRE).

anika (ML Eng): ran 5k repeat tests post-hotfix at 200 qps — variance dropped to near-zero; ranks stable across runs. Also adjusted validator to token-count post-tokenize; that should reduce unexpected 413s.

maya (CSE): Customer confirmed after pinning and hotfix: no more score swaps in their tests, 413s gone. They're still concerned about the model tokenizer change — they'd like a heads-up for future tokenization-affecting rollouts.

john (ProdEng): We'll add a rollout checklist item: run cross-tokenizer equivalence tests and notify customers of tokenizer-normalization changes for rerank models. Also adding a post-rollout smoke that does repeated identical calls to check nondeterminism.

leo (Support): Closing loop with NimbusPay now; they asked for an SLA note. I'll follow up with jira #CS-4893 linking the hotfix and actions.

maya (CSE): Thanks everyone. Marking as resolved for now; re-open if customer sees anything else.

ryan (SRE): logging the incident and RCA draft — will post in #postmortems tomorrow.

anika (ML Eng): RCA highlights: tokenizer normalization + runtime batching race -> nondeterministic rerank outputs; fixes: validator reorder, buffer reset hardening, added smoke tests.

john (ProdEng): Nice work team :thumbsup:
